newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gore says "worst time" to cut U.S. troops in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Gore says "worst time" to cut U.S. troops in Japan.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore said on Sunday the size of U.S. forces in Japan needed to be maintained, calling the present the "worst time" to reduce the current contingent.
The size of U.S. forces stationed in Japan has become a source of tension, with opponents saying many of the troops should be withdrawn from Japanese territory.
While meeting Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, Gore was asked if the United States would continue to need the same number of troops during the next decade.
"I think we need them now and for the forseeable future," Gore responded.
"In my view, this would be the worst time to have some reduction in U.S. forces here. The current level is the appropriate level," the U.S. vice president said.
About 75 percent of U.S. bases in Japan are on Okinawa, which makes up less than one percent of Japanese territory.

About 3,000 Okinawans who own land covering 362,000 sq metres (433,000 sq yards) on 12 bases including the U.S. Air Force's huge Kadena Air Base are refusing to renew leases when they expire on May 15.
Local authorities on Okinawa, where about half of the 40,000 U.S. troops in Japan are stationed, want the bases closed by 2015, an action Tokyo strongly opposes.
Gore arrived on Sunday in Japan, the first stop on a trip to Asia that includes visits to China and South Korea.
